judge.reason: The answer clearly rejects the 98% readiness and confidence claim. It cites tuning on the test set, self-grading, excluded timeouts and unchecked side effects, and it separates pass rate from confidence and reruns from independent samples, with a plausible interval of about 89–99.9%. It asks for a fresh frozen held-out representative set, executable output and state checks, a blinded and calibrated different-model judge, timeouts counted as failures, a failure taxonomy, slices, versioned configurations and uncertainty, and it claims no fabricated runs.
